questions.stem: A 42-year-old male presented with skin OPD with generalised hypopigmented patches with diminished sensation on the patch. On examination, peripheral nerves were tender and enlarged and the nasal septum was perforated. A skin biopsy was done and sent to a laboratory for diagnosis. Microbiologists identified acid-fast bacilli in groups like globi. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Leprosy
  • The history above and acid-fast stain findings are suggestive of Leprosy caused by Mycobacterium leprae.
  • leprae is acid-fast in nature and stained with the Ziehl-Neelson technique using 5% sulphuric acid. It appears as pink acid-fast bacilli arranged singly or in groups (like cigar bundles, bound together to form GLOBI).

Clinical manifestations

  • Hypopigmented or reddish patch(es) on the skin
  • Diminished sensation or loss of sensation within skin patch(es)
  • Paresthesias (tingling or numbness in the hands or feet)
  • Painless wounds or burns on the hands or feet
  • Lumps or swelling on the earlobes or face
  • Tender, enlarged peripheral nerves

Complications:

Deformities of face:

  • Leonine fancies, facial paralysis, loss of eyebrows or eyelashes, saddle nose, perforated nasal septum, corneal opacity and ulcers) and hands & feet (claw hands, wrist drops, foot drop, clawing of toes, foot inversion)


Ananthanaryan and Paniker, 12th Edition Page No. 586,587, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 535,537

questions.stem: A 54-year-old male presented with skin OPD with skin lesions. On examination, a few asymmetric hypopigmented maculopapular skin patches were seen with clearly defined margins. The ulnar nerve was tender and enlarged. The lepromin test was positive for the patient and on the the Ziehl-Neelson stain, no acid facilitation was seen the patient is having:
questions.solutionHtml:
Tuberculoid leprosy
  • Tuberculoid leprosy is the paucibacillary type with scanty bacilli in the lesions (0-1+)
  • Clinically it is presented as few (1-2) hypopigmented skin lesions with well-defined elevated margins with loss of sensation (anaesthetic patch). The lepromin test is positive in tuberculoid leprosy.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker, 12th Edition Page No. 586, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 535

questions.stem: A 63-year-old male presented with skin OPD with skin lesions. On examination, many symmetric hypopigmented nodules were seen with irregular margins. The Lepromin test was negative for the patient and on Ziehl-neelson stain acid fast bacilli with bacteriological index 6+ were seen. The patient is having:
questions.solutionHtml:
Lepromatous leprosy
  • Lepromatous leprosy is the multibacillary type with many bacilli in the lesions (4-6+) Clinically it is presented as many, hypopigmented nodules/plaque with irregular margins. Hypoesthesia is a late sign.
  • The lepromin test is negative in lepromatous leprosy.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker, 12th Edition Page No. 586, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 535

questions.stem: A 63-year-old male presented with skin OPD with skin lesions. On examination, many symmetric hypopigmented nodules were seen with irregular margins suggestive of leprosy. Which of the following test will help in diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ziehl Neelson stain
  • Smear microscopy by Ziehl Neelson stain is done to demonstrate acid-fast bacilli in the skin lesions from slit skin smear, nasal specimen or biopsy of thickened nerve.
  • leprae is acid-fast in nature and stained with the Ziehl-Neelson technique using 5% sulphuric acid.
  • It appears as bright pink acid-fast bacilli arranged singly or in groups (like cigar bundles, bound together to form GLOBI.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker, 12th Edition Page No. 587,588, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 537, 538, https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/medicine-and-dentistry/lepromin-test

questions.stem: A 63-year-old male presented with skin OPD with skin lesions. On examination, many symmetric hypopigmented nodules were seen with irregular margins suggestive of leprosy. Treatment was started for leprosy. During treatment, the patient developed painful erythematous papular nodules. Which of the following is the likely cause of the reaction?

options.label: A
options.text: Lepra reaction type l due to delayed hypersensitivity

options.label: B
options.text: Lepra reaction type l due to immune complex-mediated hypersensitivity

options.label: C
options.text: Lepra reaction type ll due to delayed hypersensitivity

options.label: D
options.text: Lepra reaction type ll due to immune complex-mediated hypersensitivity

questions.answerText: Lepra reaction type ll due to immune complex-mediated hypersensitivity
questions.solutionHtml:
Lepra reaction type ll due to immune complex-mediated hypersensitivity
  • Options C & D. Lepra reaction type ll due to immune complex-mediated (type lll) hypersensitivity usually occurs following the start of chemotherapy for leprosy. It is also called erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL).
  • The pathogenesis of ENL is due to antigen-antibody complex deposition in the skin with the subsequent activation of the complement system.
  • It is associated with high levels of TNF, which may decrease with treatment.
  • Crops of tender erythematous nodules appear with fever due to hypersensitivity resulting from antigens released by dead Lepra bacilli.
  • Type 2 reactions are typically seen in patients with lepromatous and borderline lepromatous disease because these are the two patient groups that have the highest levels of M. leprae antigens and antibodies.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker, 12th Edition Page No. 587, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 536, https://ijdvl.com/new-insights-in-the-pathogenesis-of-type-1-and-type-2-lepra-reaction/

questions.stem: A 63-year-old male presented with skin OPD with skin lesions. On examination, many symmetric hypopigmented nodules were seen with irregular margins suggestive of leprosy. Treatment was started for leprosy. Which of the following statement is not true about the treatment and prevention of Leprosy?

options.label: A
options.text: For paucibacillary leprosy, treatment should be given for 6 months.

options.label: B
options.text: WHO recommends 3 drug regimens for treatment.

options.label: C
options.text: For the Multibacillary type, follow up to be done for 2 years.

options.label: D
options.text: Dapsone, rifampicin and clofazimine are the recommended drugs.

questions.answerText: For the Multibacillary type, follow up to be done for 2 years.
questions.solutionHtml:
For the Multibacillary type, follow up to be done for 2 years.
  • For the Multibacillary type, follow up to be done annually for 5 years while for the paucibacillary type, 2 years follow-up is required.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker, 12th Edition Page No. 588, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 538
